newsitem.title: UK: Copyright Promotions takes Mr Men to America.
newsitem.headline: Copyright Promotions takes Mr Men to America.

text.p: Britian's Copyright Promotions Group said on Monday it had signed an agreement with U.S. television programmer Summitt Media Group to sell 40 half-hour episodes of "Mr Men" childrens' characters.

"The exposure will enable us to go to manufacturers and get Mr Men on a whole range of products -- bed linen, stationery, shorts, t-shirts, you name it," said Copyright managing director Richard Culley in an interview.
The Mr Men series will have a potential audience of 200 million every weekday in the United States. It will be broadcast in America from September 1997.
"Mr Men are an extremely successful property worldwide, especially in Australia and we now have all that potential in the U.S. yet to tap into," said Culley.

Finance director Philip Whitecross said in the same interview that it was too early to determine how much the deal would make for Copyright as it depended on the level of tv syndication and the take up from licensees.

The company generates its revenue by receiving non refundable advances followed by royalties per product line. The licensee benefits from a higher rate of sale from the licensed product and the licensor gains additional revenue as well as increased exposure for its character.
The Mr Men animated characters come from books by British author and illustrator Roger Hargreaves, first published in 1972. There are 45 Mr Men and 39 Little Miss characters.
CPG act as agent for character licensing in Britain and Europe by selecting the right licensees for characters owned by the licensors.
